content.intro: Learn http and browser caching through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: HTTP and Browser Caching matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines http and browser caching as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Cache-control directives; Validators and conditional requests; Public versus private responses; Static asset caching; CDN interactions. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Cache-control directives
items.text: Cache invalidation and key scope are part of correctness. Include relevant variation dimensions, use a deliberate TTL, avoid cross-user leakage, and invalidate or refresh entries after writes.
